 Order

The petitioner-accused No.3 is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.,
in Crime No. 41/2023 of Harohalli Police Station, Ramanagara registered for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC')
on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant-Sri. R.S. Chandrashekar.
2.
Heard Sri. Dayanand Hiremath., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Rahul Rai K, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'negative' for the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:21226 REASONS 4.
The petitioner being accused No.3 is seeking grant of bail on the apprehension of being arrested.
The complainant lodged the first information against accused No.1 for the offence punishable under Sections 409, 420 of IPC.

It is stated that the present petitioner is a liaison officer, who was incharge of the Mysore Sales International Limited - Ramanagara, which was leased out in favour of the Company, which in turn appointed accused Nos.1 and 2.
Accused Nos.1 and 2 used to deposit the amount collected by them as per the agreement entered into between Mysore Sales International Limited and M/s. Strategic Outsourcing Services Pvt Limited.

As liaison officer, it is the duty of the petitioner to over see the sale and also deposit of the amount by accused Nos.1 and 2.
5.

When the audit was held, it has come to the notice that from 01.04.2020 to 21.12.2021, accused Nos.1 and 2 have not deposited the amount that was due to Mysore Sales International Limited and the present petitioner NC: 2024:KHC:21226 being the liaison officer had colluded with accused Nos.1 and 2 and committed criminal breach of trust.
6. There are prima facie materials against the petitioner as well.
Serious allegations of misappropriation of public fund is alleged against this petitioner.
The FIR was registered on 15.02.2023.
The petitioner is absconding till today.
Looking to the conduct of the petitioner and seriousness of the offence, the petitioner -accused No.3 is not entitled for grant of bail.

7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
